cohort_summary: Ten quantitative validators (8 pro, 2 serious amateur, all desktop) tried to decide whether to trust Pitch Hawk's models before betting or blending them. The Data Feed is the most credible surface in the product: per-market n, model vs landed, gap, Brier skill, scenario filters, matchup splits, lock-time grading, DNP voiding and honest SAMPLE DATA and small-sample labels. Even so, it fails a pro audit. The headline Brier skill pools markets (24.5% vs 0.5-1.3% per market), 10-pt bins can't resolve HR props, there are no CIs, log loss or ECE, and nothing ties results to prices (no ROI/CLV). Model provenance is the other blocker: the version shows only in a tooltip, the Guide is a glossary rather than a model card, and it's unclear whether headline reads are trained or the BASE placeholder. Export is half-built: the board CSV lacks ids, timestamps and version, and graded history can't be exported at all. Nobody fully completed a trust-then-bet journey; the amateurs got furthest because they need less.

personas.name: Marcus Feld
personas.profile: Pro, 9 yrs, ex-quant at a trading firm. $250k roll, $2.5k unit. Pinnacle, Circa, BetOnline, Kalshi. Player props (1+ HR, Ks).
personas.goal: Decide whether to add Pitch Hawk's HR probabilities as a feature in his own HR-prop blend before tonight's slate.
journey: Opens Data Feed directly and reads the SAMPLE DATA banner. Fine, he's evaluating the instrument, not the numbers.
Sees BRIER SKILL 24.5% on All, then By market shows 0.5-1.3%. Realizes the headline pools markets, and his trust drops right away.
Clicks 1+ HR. Calibration chart collapses into two 10-pt bars; can't see the 8-25% range where his bets live.
Looks for log loss and reliability slope; finds neither. Gap '+1.4 pts' is green although that's ~12% relative under-prediction.
Searches for the model version; finds it only by hovering a Predictions tile ('Model bh_v2').
Looks for a graded export to recompute things himself. There isn't one.
Exports the HR board CSV; no player_id/game_pk, so a name-match join is needed.
personas.quote: A 24.5% skill headline over 1% per-market skill tells me nobody here has audited the scorecard, so give me the raw graded file and I'll do it myself.

pain_points.title: Headline Brier skill pools markets and overstates skill
pain_points.detail: With 'All' markets the BRIER SKILL tile reads 24.5%, but every per-market SKILL in the By-market table is 0.5-1.3% (Totals -0.2%). The reference Brier is act*(1-act) of the pooled set, so mixing 12% HR reads with 68% hit reads makes the model look like it has 20x more skill than it does in any one market. A pro spots it in seconds and stops trusting the page.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:3901-3906 derive(): base = st.act*(1-st.act) over pooled rows; tile at pitchhawk.js:3992; screen desk__data (24.5% vs By market 0.5-1.3%)
pain_points.suggested_fix: Compute skill per market and show a count-weighted mean (or hide the pooled tile when more than one market is selected); label the reference explicitly.

pain_points.title: 10-pt calibration bands collapse low-probability markets
pain_points.detail: Filtering to 1+ HR puts all 3,174 reads into two bars (0-10, 10-20); eight empty bands fill the chart. For HR props the decision lives between 8% and 25%, which this chart can't resolve. Empty bands also carry no 'no reads' label.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:4015-4030 (fixed i*10 bands, subtitle 'per 10-pt probability band'); work/c06-quant-validators/data_hr.png
pain_points.suggested_fix: Use quantile (equal-count) bins or auto-zoom the x-range to the market's probability span; offer 2-pt / 5-pt / decile toggle; label empty bands.

pain_points.title: Calibration gap is coloured by absolute points, which hides relative miscalibration
pain_points.detail: 1+ HR shows '+1.4 pts' in green ('good'), yet 13.9% vs 12.4% is 12% relative under-prediction, which flips EV on longshot props. The thresholds also differ: tiles/table use <2 good, <4 amber (gapTone) while the chart uses within 3 pts (gapBand).
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:3907-3910 gapTone vs gapBand; desk__data By market table
pain_points.suggested_fix: Show relative gap (landed/predicted ratio) or log-odds gap next to points, colour by a z-score against n, and use one threshold rule everywhere.

pain_points.title: Graded history can't be exported
pain_points.detail: Data Feed has no Export button (no export/csv/download control on the page), and the 11k graded reads are only browsable 40 at a time. Validators want to pull the full graded set to recompute calibration, blend with their own models and run their own significance tests.
pain_points.evidence: Data Feed actions: dTf,dMk,dHand,dSide,dClear,dMkRow,dTeamTile,dMore only; D_PAGE=40 pitchhawk.js:3655
pain_points.suggested_fix: Add 'Export graded CSV' that respects the current scenario filters (one row per read: ids, probability at lock, league rate, result, model_version, lock time), plus a documented /graded API.

pain_points.title: Model name/version only appears in a hover tooltip
pain_points.detail: The only provenance on the site is 'Model bh_v2.' inside the title attribute of the 7-day calibration tiles on Predictions. Data Feed, rows, row expansion, CSV and Guide never name the model, its version, training window or when it last changed, so a validator cannot tell whether the 30-day record describes the model producing today's numbers.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:1450 (tooltip only); pitchhawk.js:1394-1395 collects model_version but never renders it; Data Feed scorecard pitchhawk.js:3985-3995
pain_points.suggested_fix: Show a visible model chip (e.g. 'bh_v2 · trained thru 2026-09-30') on the Predictions header, each expanded row, Data Feed scorecard and CSV; add a version filter / split on Data Feed and a changelog entry in the Guide.

pain_points.title: Export CSV lacks IDs, timestamps, model version and inputs
pain_points.detail: The batter CSV is rank, player, team, slot, opposing_starter, game, status, probability, league_rate, lift_pts, xpa, form_30d_rate, result. It has no MLBAM player/pitcher id, game_pk, game date/time with timezone, as-of timestamp, model_version, per-PA, opp hand or venue. Joining it to their own model means fuzzy-matching names. The starter CSV has game_time '2:48 PM' with no date or tz.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:1017-1040 predCsv headers; work/c06-quant-validators/hr.csv, sp.csv
pain_points.suggested_fix: Add player_id, opp_pitcher_id, game_pk, game_date, start_utc, as_of_utc, model_version, per_pa, opp_hand, venue_id, form PA count; offer a JSON/API endpoint with documented schema.

delights: Clear 'graded once at the probability it carried when the market locked' and DNP-voided rules
By-market table with n, model, landed, gap, skill side by side

pain_points.title: Can't backtest the ranking signal (lift / probability bands) on Data Feed
pain_points.detail: Data Feed filters are timeframe, market, team, stadium, hand, side. There's no filter by lift bucket, rank on the board, or 'top-N per day', so you can't check whether the reads the board puts at the top actually do better than the rest.
pain_points.evidence: Data Feed filter bar pitchhawk.js:3920-3975 (dTf, dMk, dHand, dSide, team, park only)

pain_points.title: No ROI or CLV record against any line
pain_points.detail: Grading is purely 'landed vs predicted'. There's no record of ROI if you'd bet the model's top-lift reads at the market, and no comparison to the closing line. For this cohort, calibration without ROI/CLV can't answer 'is there money in it'.
pain_points.evidence: Data Feed has no price fields at all (pitchhawk.js:3860-3906 statOf uses probability and result only); BRIEF: /edge only for game markets and not served
pain_points.suggested_fix: Store the open and close price at lock for each graded read; add ROI at close, CLV in cents/pts, and a 'beat the close %' to the Data Feed and By-market table.

pain_points.title: Predictions calibration tiles and Data Feed don't line up or link
pain_points.detail: Predictions shows 7-day tiles (e.g. 1+ HR 41%/15%, 27 graded) while Data Feed defaults to 30 days (1+ HR 13.9%/12.4%, 3,174 graded). The windows and sources differ with no explanation, and clicking a tile does nothing (URL unchanged), so there's no path from the board to the full record.
pain_points.evidence: pitchhawk.js:1440-1480 trustTilesHtml (7d, from /board feed) vs Data Feed 30D default; tile click test in work/c06-quant-validators/s.js
pain_points.suggested_fix: Make each tile a link to #/data?tf=7&mk=<market>, use the same source for both, and state the window and n the same way on both.

pain_points.title: Ranking is by lift over league rate, not edge vs market
pain_points.detail: The default sort (LIFT) ranks how far a player is from the league average, which the books price in already. A +12 pt lift tells a pro nothing about whether the price is beatable.
pain_points.evidence: Predictions header 'ranked by lift over the league rate'; copy.js glossary 'Lift (pts)'
pain_points.suggested_fix: Once odds exist, default sort to edge vs no-vig market; until then say plainly that LIFT is not an edge.

pain_points.title: No sportsbook line, price or implied probability on props

pain_points.evidence: Predictions row desk_pred_rowopen; pitchhawk.js:1017-1040 CSV has no price column

pain_points.evidence: pitchhawk.js:4098-4140; copy.js dFeedEmpty; desk__data
pain_points.suggested_fix: When the panel's source is empty, say which source and why ('/accuracy not served here'), or hide the panel.

pain_points.title: Guide overlay stays open after navigating
pain_points.detail: With the Guide open, changing the route (hash) to Data Feed left the overlay covering the scorecard.
pain_points.evidence: work/c06-quant-validators/data_hr.png; overlay pitchhawk.js:4388-4393
pain_points.suggested_fix: Close overlays on hashchange/route change.

pain_points.title: Graded record can't be split by model version
pain_points.detail: The data layer is keyed per (day, market, model_version), but the UI merges versions. After a retrain a validator can't isolate the current model's record from the old one.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk-data.js:418 comment; pitchhawk.js:1417-1424 collects versions but only joins them into a tooltip
pain_points.suggested_fix: Add a version chip row to the Data Feed filter bar and a vertical marker on the Daily gap chart where the version changed.

delights: Per-row 'updated' timestamps and frozen-at-first-pitch rule
Explicit 'grading paused' outage copy instead of silently empty days (copy.js dOutage)

personas.name: Ravi Menon
personas.profile: Pro, 3 yrs, Bayesian modeler. $30k roll, $300 unit. Novig, ProphetX, Pinnacle. 1+ Hit props.
personas.goal: Understand what drives a 1+ Hit read (the WHY) to decide if it's independent enough from his own model to be worth blending.
journey: Predictions 1+ Hit; reads WHY: '30d H/PA .216 (82 PA) · Devers allows .232 · H2H — · slot 8 -> 3.80 xPA'.
Expands the row: sees 1+ HIT/HR/HRR, TB, 30d form, opp SP allows, game. No attribution of points.
Sees reads built on 15-19 PA 30d samples with no word on shrinkage.
Several WHY cells cut off ('Guerrero allows ...') with no tooltip.
Concludes the inputs overlap heavily with his own; no park/weather/platoon terms listed.
personas.quote: Showing me the inputs is half of it; I need to see how much each one moved the number and how hard you regress a 19-PA sample.

pain_points.title: WHY lists inputs but not how they move the number
pain_points.detail: WHY shows '30d H/PA .216 (82 PA) · Devers allows .232 · H2H — · slot 8 -> 3.80 xPA', which is useful context, but there's no attribution (how many pts came from form vs opposing SP vs slot), no regression/shrinkage disclosure for 8-19 PA samples, no park/weather/platoon terms, and the text gets cut off ('Guerrero allows ...').
pain_points.evidence: Predictions WHY column desk_pred_rowopen rows 2-25; row expansion shows raw rates only
pain_points.suggested_fix: In the row expansion, add a small waterfall: league rate -> +form -> +opp SP -> +park -> model, with the shrinkage weight and PA used for each; tooltip the full text when it's cut off.

pain_points.title: Unclear which numbers are trained and which are the BASE placeholder
pain_points.detail: The Guide says Base = 'a simple placeholder model (league rates x 30-day form)'. BASE tags sit on REST OF GAME and TB 1.5+, but the main P(1+ HIT) column has none. Is the headline number a trained model (bh_v2?) or also league x form? Not knowing this is enough to stop a pro from betting it.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:2422-2429 baseTagHtml; copy.js glossary 'Base'; desk_pred_rowopen (BASE on 31% rest-of-game and TB 51%)
pain_points.suggested_fix: Tag every number with its source model (trained/base + version) and add a Guide table: market -> model -> status -> validation record.

pain_points.title: Guide is a glossary, not a model card
pain_points.detail: The Guide defines Read, Lift, xPA, Base, Calibration and Brier skill, but has nothing on how the models are built: features, training window, regression to prior, update cadence, how reads are locked, known biases (the postseason warning sits only on Predictions), or a link to the validation record.
pain_points.evidence: copy.js:121-137 guideIntro + glossary; pitchhawk.js:4368-4369
pain_points.suggested_fix: Add a 'Methodology' tab per market: inputs, training data and dates, version history, validation metrics (Brier, log loss, ECE) with a link to the Data Feed scenario.

pain_points.title: Ranking is by lift over league rate, not edge vs market
pain_points.detail: The default sort (LIFT) ranks how far a player is from the league average, which the books price in already. A +12 pt lift tells a pro nothing about whether the price is beatable.
pain_points.evidence: Predictions header 'ranked by lift over the league rate'; copy.js glossary 'Lift (pts)'
pain_points.suggested_fix: Once odds exist, default sort to edge vs no-vig market; until then say plainly that LIFT is not an edge.

delights: WHY column surfaces sample sizes (82 PA, 49 PA) right where you need them
Per-PA to game probability via xPA is transparent and checkable

personas.name: Jordan Pike
personas.profile: Serious amateur, data-analyst day job. $5k roll, $50 unit. DraftKings, FanDuel. 1+ HR longshots.
personas.goal: Decide if the model's HR probabilities are calibrated well enough to pick 3 HR props tonight.
journey: Predictions 1+ HR tile: 41% landed vs 15% predicted (27 graded, small sample). Alarmed.
Data Feed 1+ HR 30D: 13.9% vs 12.4%, green +1.4 pts. Confused which to believe.
Calibration chart: only two bars; can't tell how 20% reads perform.
Picks 3 high-lift names, then has to look up DK prices by hand to see if any are value.
personas.quote: One page says the HR model is way off and the other says it's fine, and neither tells me the price.

pain_points.title: Predictions calibration tiles and Data Feed don't line up or link
pain_points.detail: Predictions shows 7-day tiles (e.g. 1+ HR 41%/15%, 27 graded) while Data Feed defaults to 30 days (1+ HR 13.9%/12.4%, 3,174 graded). The windows and sources differ with no explanation, and clicking a tile does nothing (URL unchanged), so there's no path from the board to the full record.
pain_points.evidence: pitchhawk.js:1440-1480 trustTilesHtml (7d, from /board feed) vs Data Feed 30D default; tile click test in work/c06-quant-validators/s.js
pain_points.suggested_fix: Make each tile a link to #/data?tf=7&mk=<market>, use the same source for both, and state the window and n the same way on both.

pain_points.title: 10-pt calibration bands collapse low-probability markets
pain_points.detail: Filtering to 1+ HR puts all 3,174 reads into two bars (0-10, 10-20); eight empty bands fill the chart. For HR props the decision lives between 8% and 25%, which this chart can't resolve. Empty bands also carry no 'no reads' label.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:4015-4030 (fixed i*10 bands, subtitle 'per 10-pt probability band'); work/c06-quant-validators/data_hr.png
pain_points.suggested_fix: Use quantile (equal-count) bins or auto-zoom the x-range to the market's probability span; offer 2-pt / 5-pt / decile toggle; label empty bands.

pain_points.title: Calibration gap is coloured by absolute points, which hides relative miscalibration
pain_points.detail: 1+ HR shows '+1.4 pts' in green ('good'), yet 13.9% vs 12.4% is 12% relative under-prediction, which flips EV on longshot props. The thresholds also differ: tiles/table use <2 good, <4 amber (gapTone) while the chart uses within 3 pts (gapBand).
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:3907-3910 gapTone vs gapBand; desk__data By market table
pain_points.suggested_fix: Show relative gap (landed/predicted ratio) or log-odds gap next to points, colour by a z-score against n, and use one threshold rule everywhere.

pain_points.title: No sportsbook line, price or implied probability on props
pain_points.detail: P(1+ HIT) 77% has nothing next to it to compare. To find value the user must tab out to their own odds screen, de-vig, and match players by name by hand.
pain_points.evidence: Predictions row desk_pred_rowopen; pitchhawk.js:1017-1040 CSV has no price column
pain_points.suggested_fix: Show best available price, no-vig fair price and edge vs book per row (and in CSV), with book name and timestamp.

delights: Plain-English Guide definitions of calibration and Brier skill
League tick on each bar makes lift easy to see

personas.name: Sofia Lindqvist
personas.profile: Serious amateur, grad student in stats. $3k roll, $25 unit. FanDuel, Kalshi. Hit props and moneylines.
personas.goal: Validate the model before tailing: check sample sizes, Brier and skill per market, then pick 2 hit props.
journey: Data Feed: reads scorecard, toggles 7D/30D, checks n under each calibration bar. Likes it.
Notices the headline Brier skill is way above every market's own; can't tell which is right from the Guide.
Filters vs LHP to find platoon edges; splits update quickly.
Switches to Predictions to pick; the record and the board aren't linked, and there's no price to judge value.
personas.quote: This is more transparent than any tout site I've seen, but the 24.5% skill number made me wonder what else is pooled.

pain_points.title: Headline Brier skill pools markets and overstates skill
pain_points.detail: With 'All' markets the BRIER SKILL tile reads 24.5%, but every per-market SKILL in the By-market table is 0.5-1.3% (Totals -0.2%). The reference Brier is act*(1-act) of the pooled set, so mixing 12% HR reads with 68% hit reads makes the model look like it has 20x more skill than it does in any one market. A pro spots it in seconds and stops trusting the page.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:3901-3906 derive(): base = st.act*(1-st.act) over pooled rows; tile at pitchhawk.js:3992; screen desk__data (24.5% vs By market 0.5-1.3%)
pain_points.suggested_fix: Compute skill per market and show a count-weighted mean (or hide the pooled tile when more than one market is selected); label the reference explicitly.

pain_points.title: Brier skill is measured against the realized mean, not the league-rate baseline the board ranks on
pain_points.detail: The board's whole pitch is LIFT over the league rate, but skill is computed against the in-sample outcome mean, which isn't known ex ante. What a quant wants is: do these reads beat the league-rate prior (the white tick) for the same spot? That number isn't anywhere.
pain_points.evidence: frontend/pitchhawk.js:3900-3906; copy.js glossary 'Brier skill' (~line 135)
pain_points.suggested_fix: Add 'skill vs league rate' (1 - Brier_model / Brier_leaguerate per read) alongside the current figure, so the value of the lift itself is graded.

pain_points.title: Predictions calibration tiles and Data Feed don't line up or link
pain_points.detail: Predictions shows 7-day tiles (e.g. 1+ HR 41%/15%, 27 graded) while Data Feed defaults to 30 days (1+ HR 13.9%/12.4%, 3,174 graded). The windows and sources differ with no explanation, and clicking a tile does nothing (URL unchanged), so there's no path from the board to the full record.
pain_points.evidence: pitchhawk.js:1440-1480 trustTilesHtml (7d, from /board feed) vs Data Feed 30D default; tile click test in work/c06-quant-validators/s.js
pain_points.suggested_fix: Make each tile a link to #/data?tf=7&mk=<market>, use the same source for both, and state the window and n the same way on both.

pain_points.title: No sportsbook line, price or implied probability on props
pain_points.detail: P(1+ HIT) 77% has nothing next to it to compare. To find value the user must tab out to their own odds screen, de-vig, and match players by name by hand.
pain_points.evidence: Predictions row desk_pred_rowopen; pitchhawk.js:1017-1040 CSV has no price column
pain_points.suggested_fix: Show best available price, no-vig fair price and edge vs book per row (and in CSV), with book name and timestamp.

delights: n under every calibration bar
Scenario filters (hand, side, park) recompute everything instantly
Honest sample-data and small-sample labelling
